how: Private language schools with native Japanese teachers run beginner courses; universities and community clubs also teach it.
NUS Centre for Language Studies runs a Level 1 Tamil course with no prerequisites (online/Saturday sessions, subsidies for citizens).
University language centres and private schools offer Spanish courses; I did not verify a specific current class.
Alliance Francaise de Singapour is the French cultural centre and runs French courses for adults.
The Goethe-Institut Singapore teaches German at all levels.
The Korean Cultural Centre in Singapore offers Korean language classes.
SADeaf runs a four-level Singapore Sign Language programme (weekday evenings, also online) open to adults.
Informal language-exchange meetups exist on Meetup-style platforms; I did not verify a specific active group.
Many English Toastmasters clubs meet in community clubs; the Bukit Timah CC club is listed on OnePA as free.
No dedicated adult public debating club verified; impromptu-speaking Table Topics at Toastmasters is the closest, plus school/university debate circuits.
NLB's LearnX programme runs volunteer-led reading communities; the Singapore Literature Book Club meets monthly at Central Library; Silent Book Club also meets monthly.
venue: Singapore Literature Book Club (NLB, Central Library)

how: The National Museum of Singapore and many other museums are open daily.
National Gallery Singapore holds large Southeast Asian art collections.
The Changi Museum covers the Japanese occupation and POW history.
NHB publishes self-guided trails (e.g. Kampong Gelam, Little India) via Roots.gov.sg.
Time Out lists multiple guided historical trails and tours in Singapore.
NLB and museums host free or cheap public talks.
Sing Lit Station runs writing programmes and workshops.
Spoken-word open-mic nights run regularly, e.g. Layl Ash-Shayr at Wardah Books; the Speak slam series started in 2013 (current status unknown).
NLB and Archives hold records and a family-history guide; Genealogy Society Singapore and FamilySearch occasionally run seminars, but no regular classes found.
venue: National Library Board family history resources

how: Fort Canning digs (2018, 2019) used about 100 public volunteers, but digs are occasional and not a standing programme.
Singapore has no ancient monuments; the oldest dug layers (Fort Canning) are around 14th century, so field schools mean travel abroad.
Practical Philosophy Meetup holds weekly discussions, and the Philosophy Cafe has run monthly at Gone Fishing Cafe (current status unclear).
Online courses are accessible from anywhere; SkillsFuture subsidises many, though this is not a Singapore-specific venue.
The Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre offers courses in Chinese cultural arts; I did not verify calligraphy classes specifically.
The Indian Heritage Centre in Little India documents South Asian heritage.
The National Archives of Singapore lets the public search records.
Science Centre Singapore is a large interactive science museum.
Many studios and community-club classes exist; I did not verify one specific class.
Pilates studios are widely available; not verified individually.
Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery's meditation hall runs meditation courses.
venue: Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery

how: Free tai chi/taiji groups meet in community clubs and parks, e.g. Linkhall Woodlands.
A free Shaolin Neijing Yizhichan Qigong class meets Wednesday mornings at Chai Chee.
venue: Ping An RN interest group (Chai Chee Rd hard court)

how: SG Cares and NVPC list many volunteering openings.
NParks' Community in Bloom supports over 2,000 resident gardening groups and community gardens.
Temples, mosques, churches and Hindu temples welcome visitors; Sri Mariamman Temple is the oldest Hindu temple.
Community fridges and food-rescue groups exist but I did not verify a specific one.
Social service agencies and schools recruit volunteer mentors; I did not verify a specific programme.
Peer-support volunteering exists via NCSS and Silver Ribbon, and Samaritans of Singapore runs a 24h hotline; I did not find open public support meetings.
Japanese-style onsen exist, e.g. Yunomori Onsen & Spa and Ikeda Spa.
The Plunge Club offers a Finnish sauna.
Spas and reflexology shops are everywhere.
Cold Plunge SG on Neil Road and The Ice Bath Club offer ice baths.
Free clubs such as Running Department CBD sessions and Singapore Runners Club hold weekly runs.
Action for Singapore Dogs and SOSD let volunteers walk and socialise dogs.
SPCA's adoption centre rehomes cats and dogs.
Dog runs inside NParks parks, e.g. Bishan Park and Punggol Waterway Park.
venue: Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park dog run

how: A2 Movements runs beginner parkour classes (trial classes listed).
Most abandoned sites are government property so solo exploration risks trespass; guided tours of off-limits sites exist.
venue: Hidden Heritage / Beyond Expeditions guided tours

how: Meetup hosts groups such as Silent Book Club Singapore.
Volunteer coastal clean-ups run regularly; not verified here.
The Sembawang Hot Spring Park is a real geothermal spring, but bathing in pools is limited to foot soaks.
AA and similar meetings are said to exist but I did not verify details.
